A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the colloidal gold test is a sensitive measure of changes in blood proteins, particularly the gamma-globulin fraction, and that the reaction patterns obtained are related directly to changes in the blood proteins and not to liver function or to the state of the colloidal sol. In
the colloidal gold test, as it has been applied in the past, is not specific for any one protein fraction and that the test is dependent upon the relative proportions of several protein fractions.
the colloidal gold sol is coagulated by the gammaglobulins, the coagulation is inhibited by the serum albumin and the serum globulin, and the coagulation time is prolonged by the serum albumins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the colloidal gold test is a good test for detecting liver damage, but the reaction curves can be misleading.
